slices.name: ws01-25-gold-ink-codemod
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 25 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD 3d80a0e (slice 24); the base for diffs is 3d80a0e. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, the acceptance table with its AC2 row (line 26) and its T1 and T2 rows (lines 57 and 58), the step 24 block (lines 620 to 651), Decisions (Tokens from step 21, line 708; Ink and grounds and The brand navy, lines 714 and 715; and from step 24, lines 717 to 720), Deviations (step 24, lines 948 to 958), Verify items (step 24, lines 1086 to 1105), Follow-ups (Dark mode on pages not converted yet, line 1200; Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS, 1214; Gold grounds in dark mode, 1216; Navy text on the tournament hero's gold tint, 1218; GOLD_BUTTON keeps text-lca-navy, 1221; and from step 24: Gold hex text is step 25's, every use of it, 1228, and StatusBadge's tones, 1229), and steps 21 to 24), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (section 1's gold rules at lines 59 and 60, the WS01 gold text clean-up at line 314, the scope-aware guard at line 343, acceptance criterion 2 at line 349, the planned tests at lines 366 to 368 and the gold ratios at lines 2076 to 2078), src/index.css (both @theme blocks at lines 34 to 176, with the gold and status utilities at lines 62 to 69; the legacy :root semantic and status tokens at lines 221 to 328, gold at 231 to 233 and --status-soon at 239; the new-look base, dark, live, scholastic and heritage blocks at lines 380, 436, 480, 528, 578 and 594, where --gold-ink is set at lines 394, 450, 494, 541, 587 and 604 and --status-soon at 400, 454, 505 and 555; the tones at lines 608 to 660), scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.ts (its exported parser: classStrings, tokensOf, parseToken, tsxFiles) with the two maps scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.map.json and scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.status.map.json (neither watches a gold class), test/unit/raw-colours.test.ts and test/unit/fixtures/raw-colours-allowlist.json (23 entries and 34 uses name step 25), test/unit/dark-spot-later.test.ts, test/unit/redesign-status-step24.test.ts (lines 212 to 216), test/unit/tokens.test.ts (lines 108 to 122 and the per-look blocks), test/unit/token-utilities.test.ts, test/unit/themeScopes.test.ts (--gold-ink in each scope), test/unit/contrast.test.ts (the gold tests at lines 77 to 109, the pairs the status map writes from line 114, and the rule that a text-status class shares its string with its own tint at lines 661 to 695), the helpers test/unit/helpers/cssTokens.ts and jsxClasses.ts (how index.css is parsed, and how class strings and their grounds are read with the TypeScript parser), src/components/StatusBadge.tsx, PageHero.tsx, FilterDropdown.tsx and MultiSelectDropdown.tsx, src/pages/NewsPage.tsx, src/areas/registration/components/RegistrationReminderButton.tsx, and the browser test harness (playwright.config.ts, test/a11y/support.ts, baseline.ts, baseline.json, dark-spot.spec.ts lines 28 to 37, dark-grounds.spec.ts, tokens.spec.ts, known-violations.json) so the flag-off baseline comparison stays green and the dark spot run credits gold text to no later step. The manifest entries for orders 24 and 26 say what this slice follows and leaves (24 left every gold hex text class to this slice; 26 maps StatusBadge's status prop to the status tokens, with the tone and on props unchanged for current callers). The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rule that gold #c8a94a is never text on a light ground): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 25) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy.

Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old, with package-lock.json updated by npm install. The branch tip is 3d80a0e (slice 24), the same commit origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries in this container, and the working tree is clean; the local main ref in this container is 4c1a466 and does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against 3d80a0e.

Build exactly this. Remove gold text on light grounds without changing anything while newLook is off. scripts/codemods/gold-ink.ts lists every text-lca-gold use (135 in 43 TSX files) with its surrounding JSX. It classifies each by its nearest ground: inside bg-lca-navy or bg-brand-navy, PageHero, Navbar, Footer, the navy hero or another dark container, the class stays; elsewhere it becomes text-gold-ink. It prints a review table to the scratchpad (not committed) and applies the changes. A person then reviews every changed line. Meaningful icons are checked by hand: the NewsPage Pinned pin gets a visible word, rendered only under newLook so the flag-off page is unchanged, and the reminder bell in RegistrationReminderButton and TournamentDetailPage gets an accessible name (not visible, so unflagged). StatusBadge's light gold tone text-[#7a5c00] moves to text-gold-ink, and PageHero's text-[#f0d07a] eyebrow on navy moves to text-gold-on-dark, each with a legacy :root value equal to the literal it replaces (add --gold-ink-badge legacy #7a5c00 if one token cannot serve both). Because --gold-ink defaults to #c8a94a under the legacy root, the swap is invisible until data-look=new.

test/unit/goldText.test.ts is the scope-aware guard, with its allowlist fixture at test/unit/fixtures/goldAllowlist.ts. It fails when:
- text-lca-gold, text-[#c8a94a], a style color '#c8a94a' or color: LCA.gold appears in TSX outside allowlisted navy or dark contexts
- #705718 appears outside heritage files and the About menu's "You are here" label entry
- #866a1e is used as text below 13px, except on the listed #fbfaf6 contexts and as the phone tab bar's current-tab bar

#c8a94a is never text on a light ground, the phone tab bar included. The WS02 entries are in the fixture now and match nothing yet. bg-lca-gold fills and GOLD_BUTTON are unaffected.

Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): About 135 uses of text-lca-gold. (Confirmed on Oct 8: 135 occurrences in 43 TSX files (136 including a comment in src/index.css). Re-checked at 3d80a0e with ripgrep over the 106 TSX files under src, counting class tokens with their variant prefixes and opacity modifiers, and cross-checked with the codemod's own parser (classStrings and tokensOf): the same 135 in 43 files, 118 plain, 16 hover:text-lca-gold and 1 text-lca-gold/90 (Navbar.tsx 233), and the one comment in src/index.css line 21. They are not all live: 2 sit in commented-out code (AnnualMeetingPage.tsx 226 and NewsPage.tsx 166), 2 in constants (StatusBadge.tsx 28, the gold tone of its navy surface, and TournamentDetailPage.tsx 38, the Upcoming tag, drawn in the navy hero) and 131 in the className strings of elements. The ground, read with the TypeScript parser from each element and the ancestors that paint a ground, and by hand where a component is drawn in another function: 51 on navy in 20 files, the 2 constants on navy, and 80 on light grounds in 32 files (34 in 18 files on a card or a muted panel, 10 in 7 on a faint gold tint of 5 to 10 per cent, 36 in 18 on the page itself). On navy: Navbar.tsx 13 (lines 140 twice, 157, 158, 182, 183, 197, 198, 233, 260, 292, 298, 299), Footer.tsx 84, 94 and 100, PageHero.tsx 66, the navy heroes and bands (TournamentManagePage.tsx 5, TournamentDetailPage.tsx 5, TournamentPairingsPage.tsx 3, AnnualMeetingPage.tsx 3, NewsPostPage.tsx 2, ClubsPage.tsx 300, TournamentsPage.tsx 531, and one each in AccountSecurityPage, AdminPage, DashboardPage, ForgotPasswordPage, LoginPage, MembershipPage, RegisterPage and ResetPasswordPage) and the two club heroes drawn with an inline navy and marked data-ground="dark" (ClubDetailPage.tsx 150, 176, 181 and 187; AdminClubPage.tsx 275 and 302). All 16 hover forms and the one /90 are on navy, and none sits on an opaque gold fill. No TSX file names bg-lca-navy any more (step 23 renamed it bg-brand-navy), so the grounds to read are bg-brand-navy, the PageHero, Navbar and Footer components, data-ground="dark" and an inline navy style. The element and its ancestors do not show the navy for 8 tokens: NavLinkItem (Navbar.tsx 182 and 183), DrawerLink (197 and 198) and the button of MoreMenu (140, two tokens) are functions drawn inside the navy header, and the two constants; the script and the guard need an allowlist entry or a component rule for them. The 80 on light grounds are in TournamentsPage 12, DashboardPage 6, AdminClubPage 5, AdminEmailPage 5, ScholasticPage 5, ScannerPage 4, TournamentManagePage 4, ClubDetailPage 3, ContactPage 3, HomePage 3, NewsPage 3, TournamentWizard 2, AnnualMeetingPage 2, BoardPage 2, ChampionsPage 2, ClubsPage 2, MembershipPage 2, and one each in AdminAnnouncementPanel, AuditLogPanel, BoardSeatsPanel, PostsPanel, ClubLocationPicker, PrizeWinners, FamilyCard, FamilyRegistrationPanel, RegistrationReminderButton, the social feed component in src/components (line 238), AccountSecurityPage, DonationSuccessPage, MembershipSuccessPage, SupportPage and TournamentPairingsPage. Every one of the 80 is an icon (a pin, a map marker, a calendar, a person, a trophy and the like) beside words in another colour; not one is words. So the light-ground gold of AC2 is gold icons, which need 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) rather than 4.5:1. Brand gold is 2.28:1 on white. Under the new look --gold-ink is #866a1e: 5.13:1 on white, 4.83:1 on the muted ground #f7f8fa, 4.76:1 or better on the 10 per cent gold tints behind these icons, #705718 in heritage (6.18:1 on its paper #f7f3e8) and #c8a94a in dark mode and the live look (7.64:1 on #111a2c). Words in --gold-ink on a gold tint of 20 or 25 per cent would fall to 4.42:1 and 4.26:1, so the contrast test should hold icons (3:1) and words (4.5:1) apart and fail a words use on a tint of 20 per cent or more.) Meaningful gold icons. (NewsPage.tsx:140 <Pin className="size-3 text-lca-gold" aria-label="Pinned" /> on a light ground; Bell icons in RegistrationReminderButton.tsx:83 and TournamentDetailPage.tsx. Re-checked: NewsPage.tsx line 140 is that line, in a bg-card link, and it already has aria-label="Pinned", so a screen reader hears the word and a sighted visitor sees only the icon; PostsPanel.tsx line 155 is the same pin with the same label in the admin list, also on a bg-card; NewsPostPage.tsx line 57 draws a pin with the visible word Pinned on the navy hero and needs nothing. The reminder bell at RegistrationReminderButton.tsx 83 sits inside a Button whose words are Notify me when it opens (BellOff and Remove notification in the other branch), and the icon package (version 1.25.0, its Icon module, line 36) sets aria-hidden on an icon that has no label or title, so the bell is decorative beside its words and already needs no accessible name; TournamentDetailPage.tsx has Bell and BellOff at lines 1062 and 1064 with no gold class and the same visible words. So the manifest's reminder bell gets an accessible name has nothing to fix: record what was checked, and do not add a label that would make a screen reader say the words twice. The pin's gap is the visible word. It renders only under newLook, and with newLook off the markup stays as it is (the aria-label stays): the precedents are FEATURES.newLook in Footer.tsx line 115 and the test pair that mocks src/lib/features, appearance-control.test.tsx (line 16) with appearance-control-off.test.tsx; with the word shown the icon takes aria-hidden so the word is not read twice. Decide whether PostsPanel's pin gets the same word, and record it.) Other gold-ish text. (StatusBadge light gold uses text-[#7a5c00]; PageHero eyebrow uses text-[#f0d07a] on navy. Re-checked: StatusBadge.tsx 35 and PageHero.tsx 75 are those two strings, and they are two of 34 gold hex text classes in 20 files, which the step 24 records give to this slice whole (Follow-ups, line 1228: it takes every allowlist entry whose reason names step 25). text-[#7a5c00] is 28 uses in 16 files (27 plus hover:text-[#7a5c00] in MemberSeatsCell.tsx 78): AuditLogPanel.tsx 40, 63, 68, 69, 71 and 77; BoardSeatsPanel.tsx 126 and 327; MemberSeatsCell.tsx 57 and 78; MembersTable.tsx 135; TournamentList.tsx 17; TournamentWizard.tsx 373 and 503; ResultsEntry.tsx 92 and 107; FilterDropdown.tsx 50; MultiSelectDropdown.tsx 62; StatusBadge.tsx 35; AdminEmailPage.tsx 95 and 498; BoardInboxPage.tsx 231, 232 and 375; BoardPage.tsx 158; ChampionsPage.tsx 96; TournamentsPage.tsx 644; WorkspacePage.tsx 76. 24 of the 28 are dark gold words on a gold tint of 8 to 20 per cent (21 in their own string with bg-lca-gold at /8, /10, /15, /18 or /20, and BoardInboxPage's 3 in a parent that has one); 4 are not on a tint (ResultsEntry.tsx 92 and 107, the count of results missing, on the page; ChampionsPage.tsx 96, a label on a bg-card; MemberSeatsCell.tsx 78, the hover colour of a dashed pill). text-[#f0d07a] is 5 in 5 files, each on a gold tint of 15 or 20 per cent over a ground that stays dark in every look: PageHero.tsx 75 (the eyebrow pill on the navy hero), ContactPage.tsx 61 (the same pill on the navy hero of /contact), FilterDropdown.tsx 47 and MultiSelectDropdown.tsx 59 (the on-navy branch of the chosen filter), HomePage.tsx 89 (the pill over the hero photo's dark veil, marked data-ground="dark", with a backdrop blur). text-[#8a6d1f] is 1: ClubDetailPage.tsx 43, the Upcoming badge on its 15 per cent gold tint, 4.38:1 in today's look, below 4.5:1, which newLook off must keep.)

Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at 3d80a0e. One token cannot serve all of them, and two of the manifest's token names do not fit: the legacy :root gives --gold-ink and --gold-on-dark the brand gold #c8a94a (index.css 232 and 233, held to it by tokens.test.ts lines 110 to 113), so text-lca-gold to text-gold-ink changes nothing with newLook off, but text-[#7a5c00] to text-gold-ink would turn StatusBadge's dark gold words (5.39:1 on their tint) into #c8a94a (about 2:1), text-[#f0d07a] to text-gold-on-dark would turn PageHero's pill words into #c8a94a, and #8a6d1f has no token. So each of the three literals needs a token whose plain :root value is that literal (or stays raw in the allowlist with a reason), as the manifest allows with --gold-ink-badge for #7a5c00. --status-soon is exactly #7a5c00 on the legacy :root (line 239; #705718 in the light looks at lines 400 and 555, #c8a94a in dark at 454, #f3f5f9 in live at 505), but contrast.test.ts lines 661 to 695 fail any text-status class whose string lacks its own opaque tint, Decisions line 717 says never a status word without its tint, and the pages' tints are bg-lca-gold at /8 to /20, not --status-soon-tint (legacy colour-mix 20 per cent, line 240), so it cannot be used without changing a rule or today's tint; decide and record. Any token you add goes inside the existing @theme inline block (token-utilities.test.ts requires exactly two @theme blocks), has its plain :root value in tokens.test.ts, and has a new-look value in every block that sets --gold-ink, because scholastic (always light) and live (always dark) ignore the device setting and would otherwise inherit the wrong one from <html>: base light, dark inside @media screen, live inside @media screen, scholastic; heritage restyles --gold-ink only and inherits the rest. Values that read: dark gold words on a gold tint #705718 in the light looks (5.69:1 or better up to a 25 per cent tint) and #c8a94a in dark and live (4.73:1 or better up to 25 per cent over #111a2c); the pill words on a tint over the navy that stays #1a2744 in every look read 6.87:1 to 7.63:1 as #f0d07a and 4.52:1 to 5.02:1 as #c8a94a, so measure the home hero pill over its photo before choosing. #8a6d1f: decide between a token of its own, and keeping it raw with its reason; do not move it to the #7a5c00 token, which changes today's look. themeScopes.test.ts gets the new tokens in each scope, as it has --gold-ink. The scope is wider than the manifest says: it names StatusBadge and PageHero only; the step 24 records take all 34 gold hex classes and the allowlist's 23 entries naming step 25 (the 34 uses in 20 files) go with them. Pins that follow: raw-colours.test.ts counts the allowlist at 44 hex, 34 veils and 13 StatusBadge, print-page and dot classes (91 uses, lines 164 and 165) and pins seven hex colours (lines 203 to 206), which become 10 hex classes in 7 files (#9b1c1c 2, #1e4d7b 2, #1877f2 4, #f2efe6 2; 57 uses in all) and four colours, and the allowlist file's own comment drops the gold sentence; dark-spot-later.test.ts reads the allowlist's step 25 entries (lines 56 to 64), checks the spec's list with text-lca-gold (line 53) and sorts the entries that are not later (lines 92 to 111), and test/a11y/dark-spot.spec.ts LATER (lines 33 to 37) then credits only StatusBadge's seven light tones, so text-lca-gold on navy that fails contrast would fail the spec; redesign-status-step24.test.ts lines 212 to 216 derive 34 and 20 from those entries for the follow-up line, which says 34 in 20, so pin the numbers instead; tokens.test.ts line 121 pins the string gold: 'bg-lca-gold/20 text-[#7a5c00]' in StatusBadge. Never rename or remove a follow-up: close the step 24 gold follow-up, GOLD_BUTTON and Dark mode on pages not converted yet by adding Done in step 25 to them. The maps and the ratchet: neither map watches a gold class, so neither changes. scripts/codemods/gold-ink.ts is new and can import the parser the other script exports. The grammar, since step 24, names a hex class in watch and in a rule's from, and a rule writes a plain utility, so the 34 hex classes (which need no ground, since the same token serves any ground they sit on) can move by a third map run with --map, or inside gold-ink.ts; the ground-aware text-lca-gold rewrite cannot be a rule, since a rule sees one string and the ground is in the ancestors. Decide and record which; whichever runs needs its own --check in a test (the status map's runs in semantic-map.test.ts, its describe at line 756, and in semantic-colours-edges.test.ts at lines 126 and 234), and a proof that every class it writes resolves under the legacy :root to the colour it replaced, compiled as semantic-map.test.ts does from line 569, with a merge check for the written text colours. The ratchet reads only the two maps' keep entries (raw-colours.test.ts line 122) and counts text-lca-navy, bg-white, palette and hex classes: gold classes are not raw to it, so text-lca-gold on navy is the gold guard's, not the ratchet's. The guard as the manifest describes it meets a tree that lacks its subjects: text-[#c8a94a] is used 0 times; a literal style colour of #c8a94a 0 times (the two #c8a94a literals in TSX are a placeholder, AdminClubPage.tsx 395, and a swatch's fallback background, AdminPage.tsx 532); color: LCA.gold is never a text colour (AdminClubPage.tsx 77, 112 and 252 are the club colour field's default); #705718 appears only in a comment (ScopeFixturePage.tsx 42) and #866a1e only in a comment (src/lib/brand.ts 12); #fbfaf6 appears nowhere; there is no About menu 'You are here' label (LCAMap.tsx's 'You are here' is a map marker's title) and no phone tab bar (the two 'Tab bar' comments, TournamentManagePage.tsx 1113 and AdminClubPage.tsx 292, are page tabs). The WS02 entries therefore match nothing, and the test should say so and fail if one starts to match without its context. No TSX file is a heritage file: the heritage pages are the six routes in HERITAGE_ROUTES (src/lib/themeScopes.ts line 43), AboutPage, BoardPage, BylawsPage, MinutesPage, AnnualMeetingPage and ChampionsPage, so define heritage files from that list. The guard should also fail the other way: a gold-ink token class inside a navy ground (about 2:1 in the light look). The existing allowlist fixtures are JSON (raw-colours-allowlist.json) and the manifest names test/unit/fixtures/goldAllowlist.ts; follow the manifest and keep an entry as file, class, count and reason. A gold text colour that is not a literal: a club's own colour is text in ClubDetailPage.tsx 236, 290 and 332 (bg-card) and ClubsPage.tsx 73 (an aria-hidden monogram on a 16 per cent tint) through style={{ color }}, where color is club.color || LCA_GOLD (constants at ClubDetailPage.tsx 22 and ClubsPage.tsx 18), so a club with no colour shows gold words on white at 2.28:1 and a literal scan never sees it. Decide whether the fallback for text becomes var(--gold-ink) (the same #c8a94a with newLook off) or stays as user data as step 24 decided for club colours, and have the guard read it either way. Not text and not moved, to be recorded as follow-ups: bg-lca-gold 155 in 54 files, border-lca-gold 78 in 36, ring-lca-gold 6 in 5 (ClubsPage.tsx 126 and ScannerPage.tsx 869 draw focus rings in brand gold on light grounds at 2.28:1, and MiniCalendar.tsx 77 draws today's ring), border-l-lca-gold 4, divide-lca-gold 1 and decoration-lca-gold 1 (Navbar.tsx 44, on navy). The gold link State champions (TournamentsPage.tsx 531) is gold on the navy hero with no underline until hover, so colour alone sets it apart from the words around it, and the accessibility checker's link-in-text-block finds it (as the step 23 and 24 records say); it stays text-lca-gold on navy, and the nothing-relies-on-colour-alone line must say that it is left. GOLD_BUTTON in src/lib/brand.ts line 36 still carries text-lca-navy (the same fixed navy as text-brand-navy; not a TSX file, so out of every scan); the manifest says GOLD_BUTTON is unaffected and the step 23 follow-up (line 1221) says it moves with this step or when the file is next changed: decide, and if it moves, run semantic-map-cascade.test.ts and semantic-map-grounds.test.ts, which read the string through goldButton(). StatusBadge is step 26's file: here only its light gold tone's words change (line 35) and its navy tone (line 28) stays text-lca-gold on navy, with the keep entries for the file and its allowlist lines for step 26 untouched. Lint: 13 errors and 13 warnings at 3d80a0e, measured with npm run lint; the errors are in functions/api/support.ts 1, functions/api/support/[id].ts 1, functions/utils/live/swiss/matching.ts 2, scanner/sandbox/chess-shim/src/index.ts 4, scanner/sandbox/genGames.ts 4 and scanner/sandbox/perft.ts 1, none in a file this slice has a reason to touch; the 13 warnings are in BoardSeatsPanel, ChampionsPanel, PostsPanel, TournamentWizard, LCAMap, FamilyCard, FamilyRegistrationPanel, UscfSearchInput, HomePage (2), ScholasticPage and TournamentsPage (2). Build size: step 24 recorded dist/assets CSS 121,540 bytes (one file) and JavaScript 2,567,800 bytes in 104 files, 127 files in all, and the dist folder in this container holds exactly those; report the sizes before and after. The stylesheet build reads every file in the repository for class names (index.css sets no @source; follow-up line 1214), so a test, map or record that spells out text-[#7a5c00] or the other old classes keeps their rules in the CSS: build the planted class names in tests when the test runs, and report the CSS growth. The dark spot run: step 24's one failure left on /tournaments, the LCA pill (TournamentsPage.tsx 644, text-[#7a5c00] on its gold tint, 1.84:1 in dark mode, #7a5c00 on #3d392b), clears only if this slice moves that class; quote the run. The WS01 deviations list (REDESIGN_SPEC.md line 112) carries a sentence per step up to step 24: add step 25's if the slice deviates, which it does by taking all 34 gold hex classes and by adding tokens.

Gate before reporting: npm run lint (baseline 13 errors and 13 warnings, measured on this tree; the error total never rises from 13 and every error in a touched file is fixed; report before and after), npm run build, npm run typecheck:functions, npm run check:bundle, npm run test:all (unit 2770 in 107 files and integration 790 in 58 files before this slice; report the counts), and then PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y end to end in this container with its output quoted (both builds, the flag-off baseline compared and unchanged, the dark spot run's results; 125 passed and 30 skipped before this slice). test/a11y/baseline.json must not be rewritten: with newLook off nothing visible changes, and a baseline difference is a defect in the slice. If an integration file fails to load as a whole on the first run, rerun that file alone once before treating it as real. Standing rules: no AI references anywhere, in code, code comments, docs or commit text; read the real file before changing it; match repo conventions; WCAG 2.2 AA; plain language ('US Chess', a weekday on every date, '7:00 PM'); no em dashes in anything you write; fixtures contain nothing real; new packages exact-pinned. The recorder updates REDESIGN_STATUS.md (a step 25 block after step 24's and the Last updated line; the AC2 row of the acceptance table, replacing Planned with the proofs in the pattern of the T2 row; decisions; deviations; the judgement calls; each resolved verify item; the counts; and the follow-ups this step closes, by adding Done in step 25 to them and never renaming or removing one, because test/unit/redesign-status-step23.test.ts and redesign-status-step24.test.ts pin their headings) and, if the slice deviates from the brief, the step 25 sentence in the WS01 deviations list of docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md, and drafts the commit text into <scratchpad>/slice25-commit.txt: a subject under 72 characters and plain prose, no attribution or co-author lines, no session links, no em dashes. The step records, the acceptance table and Decisions must not use the words slice, builder, scout, planner, recorder, manifest, subagent, workflow or the phrase the lead.
